llm.label: generate()
llm.title: How a language model turns a prompt into an answer
llm.answer: A computer engineer focused on AI and MLOps.
llm.description: Diagram of how a language model writes an answer. It receives the prompt “Who is Santiago Die?”, splits it into tokens with their ids, turns each token into a vector with its position, passes the vectors through stacked attention layers, scores every possible next token, samples one, turns it back into text and feeds it back as input. One token at a time, it writes: “A computer engineer focused on AI and MLOps.”
llm.note: Illustrative values; the token ids are real (cl100k_base tokenizer).

stages.label: prompt
stages.text: The question arrives as plain text.

stages.label: tokens
stages.text: A tokenizer cuts it into tokens and maps each one to a fixed id.

stages.label: embeddings
stages.text: Each id becomes a vector of numbers, combined with its position.

stages.label: attention
stages.text: Attention layers weigh how much each token matters to the others, block after block.

stages.label: softmax
stages.text: The last layer scores every possible next token; softmax turns the scores into probabilities.

stages.label: sampling
stages.text: One token is drawn from those probabilities; the temperature sets how adventurous the choice is.

stages.label: output
stages.text: The chosen id turns back into text and joins the answer.

stages.label: loop
stages.text: The new token goes back into the input and the cycle repeats until the end token.
